events.text: The ferry you crossed as a youth is gone. A stone bridge stands there now, its rails worn smooth by hands. At its foot an old man roasts chestnuts. He has the ferryman's nose, the same crooked one. The ferryman used to charge you double because you were rude.

choices.text: Buy chestnuts and ask about the ferry

effects.log: "Great-grandfather? Grumpy man. Charged rude people double." You pay double. It feels like settling a debt.

choices.text: Cross the river on the water, for old times

effects.log: Halfway across you remember the bridge is right there. Three children watch you with their mouths open. One of them claps.

choices.text: Sit under the bridge and listen

effects.log: The river sounds the same. That is the only thing that does. You stay until the chestnut man packs up.

events.text: In a teahouse a storyteller slaps his fan on the table. Tonight's tale is about you. In his version you are nine feet tall, you eat iron for breakfast, and you won a famous duel with a shout. You won it with a pebble, and you were sitting down.

choices.text: Correct him from the back of the room

effects.log: The whole teahouse turns to look at you. "And who are you, old one?" Nobody believes a word. The shout stays in.

choices.text: Tip him five taels to make you taller

effects.log: By the last bell you are eleven feet tall and your shout splits a mountain. The crowd loves it. So, quietly, do you.

choices.text: Drink your tea and leave a pebble on the table

effects.log: The storyteller finds the pebble later. He looks at it for a long time. Next week the tale has a pebble in it.

events.text: The boulder behind the old village still carries the dent of your fist. You made it at nineteen, after a bad day. Children have polished it smooth. They slide down it and call it the Giant's Bowl. One of them asks if you want a turn.
events.arc: The Rock With the Fist In It

choices.text: Punch it again, a little to the left

ok.log: A second bowl, deeper than the first. The children cheer. You have improved, which is something after all these years.

fail.log: The rock has grown harder, or you have grown older. Your knuckles say the second. (-5 health)

choices.text: Take a turn sliding down

effects.log: It is a very good slide. You understand why nobody has filled it in.

choices.text: Sit beside it and remember the bad day

effects.log: You cannot remember what made you so angry. Only the dent remains. That seems about right.

events.text: A persimmon tree stands at the crossroads, broad as a house. You spat the seed there yourself, a long time ago. Now the village calls it the Grandfather Tree. Strips of cloth hang from every branch, each a prayer. Some of the fruit has gone soft at the heart.

choices.text: Eat one persimmon

effects.log: It is the sweetest persimmon you have eaten. You feel you have earned it more than most.

choices.text: Draw the rot out of the trunk with qi

effects.log: The old wood drinks your qi like a thirsty mule. Next autumn the village will say the Grandfather Tree had a good year.

choices.text: Tie a cloth of your own

effects.log: You do not know who you are praying to. Perhaps to the tree. It owes you one.

events.text: Rain catches you on the road. You share a roadside pavilion with a peddler and his mule. The mule eats your hat brim. The peddler apologises, then offers you a rice ball, then tries to sell you tea. The rain does not stop.

choices.text: Share the rice balls and talk

effects.log: He talks about prices, his knees, and a daughter who married well. You talk about nothing. It is a fine afternoon.

choices.text: Breathe with the rain

effects.log: Drip, drip, the eaves; hiss, the road. Your breath falls in with it. The peddler thinks you are asleep.

choices.text: Buy his tea (3 taels)

effects.log: Too expensive. Very good. The mule watches you drink it with deep interest.

events.text: A swordsman of nineteen blocks the mountain path. He has a new sword, a new robe and no manners. He calls you "old timer" and tells you to step aside, a hero is passing. He has no idea who you are. Neither, these days, does anyone.

choices.text: Step aside and bow

effects.log: He passes with his chin up. You hope the mountain teaches him what you did not bother to.

choices.text: Take his sword with two fingers

effects.log: You hand it back hilt first. He stares at his empty hand, then at you, then runs. By evening there is a rumour.

choices.text: Point out the flaw in his footwork

effects.log: He argues. Then he tries it your way. Then he is very quiet. He steps aside for you.

events.text: The plain where two armies met is barley now. The wind runs over it like a hand on a dog's back. A farmer is turning the soil. His hoe rings on something. A rusted arrowhead. He holds it up and asks what it is.

choices.text: Tell him what happened here

effects.log: He listens to the whole thing leaning on his hoe. Then he says the barley grows well here. You both look at the field.

choices.text: Buy the arrowhead from him (2 taels)

effects.log: It is lighter than you remember them being. Everything about that day was heavier.

choices.text: Bow to the field

effects.log: The farmer, puzzled, bows too. Somewhere under the barley someone is not alone.

events.text: A wild ginseng grows from a crack halfway up a cliff. Its red berries say it is at least a century old. A hawk has a nest beside it and an opinion about you.

choices.text: Leap up and take it

ok.log: One kick off the stone, one hand on the root, one hawk furious. You come down with dirt on your sleeve and a century in your fist.

fail.log: The hawk strikes your ear on the way up. You land in a bush. The ginseng watches. (-8 health)

choices.text: Leave it to finish growing

effects.log: Another century and it will be a better root. You might even be around.

events.text: A bowl of noodles cost two coppers when you were young. The noodle stall here asks one whole tael. You check the sign three times. The cook asks if you are going to eat or just read.

choices.text: Pay and eat (1 tael)

effects.log: They are good noodles. Not a tael good. But good.

choices.text: Explain what noodles used to cost

effects.log: You explain for some time. The cook explains back, about flour and rents. You both learn something. You do not get noodles.

choices.text: Catch a fish and cook it by the river

effects.log: The fish costs nothing. The fire costs nothing. The smoke in your eyes is free as well.

events.text: The first snow comes down on a mountain pass you crossed at twenty, running from someone. The trail is gone under white. Nobody is chasing you now. The silence is so complete you can hear the flakes land.

choices.text: Walk the pass slowly, the whole way

effects.log: You leave one line of footprints. By the next morning the snow has taken it back.

choices.text: Build a snowman of the one who chased you

effects.log: It has his scowl exactly. You give it a stick sword. It looks better than he ever did.

choices.text: Find the cave you hid in

effects.log: The cave is smaller than you remember. Your initials are still on the wall, carved badly, by a frightened young person.

events.text: You dug this well for a village, once, in a dry year. The village moved down to the river long ago. The well is dry. A crow sits on its rim and looks at you as if you should do something.

choices.text: Dig it deeper with your bare hands

ok.log: Water rises by evening. A shepherd finds it the next day. By spring there is a hut beside it, then two.

fail.log: You hit rock, then harder rock. The crow leaves, disappointed. (-5 health)

choices.text: Drop a coin in for whoever comes next

effects.log: It clinks on stone. Even a dry well likes to be asked.

events.text: A boy riding an ox stops in the road and stares. His grandmother, he says, told stories about a stranger with your face who killed a tiger with a spoon. Are you a ghost? The ox chews and waits for the answer.

choices.text: Say yes, a very old ghost

effects.log: He screams with joy and gallops off, as much as an ox gallops. You will be a ghost in that village for another century.

choices.text: Ask his grandmother's name

effects.log: You remember her. A girl with a runny nose who held the spoon. It was a ladle, actually.

choices.text: Give him a copper and go

effects.log: He bites the copper to check it. A sensible child. The ox is less impressed.

events.text: You reach a summit before dawn. Below you the valleys are full of cloud, white and slow as milk. The peaks stand out of it like islands. Then the sun comes up and sets the whole sea on fire.

choices.text: Breathe in the first light

effects.log: It goes down like warm broth. The clouds roll. For a moment you are the only person awake in the world.

choices.text: Just watch

effects.log: You do not cultivate. You do not think. You watch, the way you did when you were small and the sky was new.

events.text: A summer night. The frogs are shouting. Over the paddies the fireflies come up in their thousands, soft green lights drifting. A farmer's child runs among them with a gauze bag. You were that child, somewhere, once.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and watch them

effects.log: Each one is on, then off. A whole life is not much longer, seen from far enough.

choices.text: Help the child catch a bagful

effects.log: You are very good at it. The child declares you a master. Of fireflies. It is a better title than some.

events.text: Three bandits block the gorge and ask for a toll. The leader has a scar on his chin and his grandfather's voice. You spared that grandfather here. He was blocking this same gorge. Some families are in the trade.

choices.text: Pay their toll (10 taels)

effects.log: They are surprised you pay. So are you. You tell them their grandfather was better at it.

choices.text: Tell them about their grandfather

effects.log: They listen, then they argue, then the youngest cries a little. They let you pass for free. They say they will think about farming.

choices.text: Take their toll box off them

ok.log: Twenty taels and a lesson. The grandfather's lesson, again. It does not seem to take.

fail.log: They fight harder than their grandfather did. You win, but your ribs complain all evening. (-6 health)

events.text: A donors' stele outside a temple lists the people who paid for its rebuilding, a lifetime ago. Your name is there, near the top. It is spelled wrong. It has been spelled wrong, in stone, ever since.

choices.text: Pay a mason to fix it (8 taels)

effects.log: The mason fixes it. The new strokes are whiter than the old. Now it looks like you came back to brag.

choices.text: Leave it. That person is dead anyway

effects.log: Whoever that misspelled person was, they gave generously. You decide to think well of them.

choices.text: Donate again under the wrong name

effects.log: The monk writes it down exactly as the stele has it. Now there are two of them.

events.text: The river changed its course decades ago. The town where you once ate the best dumplings of your life is under it now. On a clear day you can see roof tiles on the riverbed, and the top of the town gate, green with weed.

choices.text: Dive down and look

ok.log: In the silt of the old shrine you find a little statue. It still has a dumpling offering's stain on it. You take it up into the light.

fail.log: The current is stronger than it looks. You come up coughing, with weed in your hair and nothing in your hands. (-6 health)

choices.text: Float a lantern over the roofs

effects.log: It drifts over the gate, the market, the dumpling shop. Then the river takes it somewhere else.

events.text: A little shrine sits under a pine. Inside is a crude statue holding a sword the way you hold a sword, which is wrong, and which you never fixed. The villagers say the mountain god walks the ridge at night. You used to.

choices.text: Sweep the shrine and straighten the offerings

effects.log: In the morning the villagers find it swept. That week the mountain god is very popular.

choices.text: Eat the rice cake offering

effects.log: It is yours, in a sense. It is also a little stale. The statue watches. You feel judged by yourself.

choices.text: Carve the sword grip correctly

effects.log: Now the statue holds it right. It looks less like you. That is probably an improvement.

events.text: A temple on the hill keeps a fat orange cat. The monk says the temple has always had an orange cat. You remember the first one. It stole your fish. This one sits on your foot and looks at your fish.

choices.text: Give it the fish

effects.log: It eats with the confidence of a dynasty. Some lines go on longer than kingdoms.

choices.text: Eat the fish yourself, slowly

effects.log: The cat watches every bite. The monk says it will remember you. You believe it.

events.text: In a market a young porter drops a crate and laughs at himself. You stop walking. It is your sworn brother's laugh, the exact one, dead these many years. The same gap in the teeth. The same ears. He has no idea why the stranger is staring.

choices.text: Help him pick up the crate

effects.log: His name is the same family name. Of course it is. He thanks you and asks if you want work. You say maybe.

choices.text: Ask about his family

effects.log: Porters, mostly. A great-great-grandfather who was some kind of fighter, they say. Nobody remembers his name. You do.

choices.text: Walk on before he looks up

effects.log: Some faces you should not chase. You buy a pear you do not want and keep walking.

events.text: The porter from the market has entered a town martial contest. He fights like a man who learned from a bad book. His opponent is bigger, trained, and cruel. In the stands you can see the move that is coming. The boy cannot.

choices.text: Flick a seed at the big one's knee

effects.log: The big one slips. The boy wins by accident and cannot stop grinning. Nobody saw. That is the point.

choices.text: Let him lose, then teach him that evening

effects.log: He loses badly. That night you show him three steps. They are his ancestor's steps. He learns them like he always knew them.

choices.text: Let him lose and say nothing

effects.log: He loses, gets up, bows, and laughs. That laugh again. He will be fine.

events.text: The porter's family house is falling down. While helping fix the roof, you find a box in the rafters. Inside is a letter, never sent, addressed to you. Your sworn brother wrote it the year he died. The ink is brown now.

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: It says he is sorry about the argument. It says the debt is forgiven, both ways. It says he hopes you live a long time. You did.

choices.text: Give it to the boy to keep

effects.log: He reads it aloud, badly. He asks who the letter is for. You tell him it is for someone who got it.

choices.text: Burn it unread, as an offering

effects.log: The smoke goes straight up on a still day. Whatever it said, it has arrived.

events.text: The hamlet you were born in had eleven houses and one dog. It is a walled town now, with a tax office and a drum tower. The guard at the gate asks your business. You say you were born here. He laughs. He has heard that one.

choices.text: Pay the gate fee like a stranger (2 taels)

effects.log: You are a stranger. It is true. You walk in under a gate where the dog used to sleep.

choices.text: Go over the wall at night

effects.log: The wall is new. The stars above it are not. You land in a cabbage patch that used to be the road.

choices.text: Look at it from the hill and go

effects.log: From up here you can almost see the eleven houses inside it. Almost.

events.text: You find the spot. The house you were born in is a tofu shop now. A woman is pressing curds where the kitchen was. The old stone step is still there, the one you cracked by jumping off the roof. She asks if you want tofu.

choices.text: Buy tofu and eat it on the step

effects.log: It is good tofu. The step is cold. You sit there until she asks you, kindly, to move for customers.

choices.text: Tell her about the roof

effects.log: She laughs and shows you the crack. Her children have a story about it too. In theirs, it was a dragon.

choices.text: Leave a pouch of taels under the step (10 taels)

effects.log: She will find it when the step finally breaks. Maybe in a century. You will know.

events.text: A hermit is fishing with a line that has no hook. His beard is in the water. You try to read his realm and slide off him like rain off oiled paper. He tells you to sit down; you are scaring the fish he is not catching.

choices.text: Sit and fish beside him

effects.log: By sunset you have caught nothing. You understand why that matters, and you could not say it in words.

choices.text: Ask him how old he is

effects.log: He counts on his fingers, gives up, and says he was old when the river was a stream. You think he might be joking. You hope so.

choices.text: Ask for one move

ok.log: He lifts the hookless line out of the water. The drops hang in the air and do not fall. You stay three days thinking about it.

fail.log: He lifts the line. Nothing happens. He says that is the move. You will be angry about it for a decade.

events.text: A troupe of players sets up in a village square. The play is about you. In it you defeat a dragon by sneezing on it. The actor playing you wears a beard to his knees and a mask with three eyebrows. The children love it.

choices.text: Clap louder than anyone

effects.log: The actor bows to you directly. You bow back. The dragon, two men in a sheet, bows as well.

choices.text: Go backstage and fix his stance

effects.log: The next night the sneeze is still in, but the stance is perfect. A master in the crowd notices and goes very pale.

choices.text: Sneeze, quietly, at the climax

effects.log: The banners flap. A hat flies off. The crowd decides it was part of the show.

events.text: At a wayside inn a young master sits in the best seat. Twenty-five and already close to your realm. People bow as he passes. He looks at you and decides you are some elder of no reputation. He asks you to fetch his tea.

choices.text: Fetch his tea

effects.log: You pour it perfectly. He notices the cup did not ring once. He does not ask. He will think about it for years.

choices.text: Ask for a friendly spar

ok.log: He is good. You are older. It ends in one exchange. He sits down and pours you tea, without being asked.

fail.log: He is very good. You win, but only just, and your elbow will remember it. So will he. (-10 health)

choices.text: Tell him his left meridian is blocked

effects.log: He laughs. Then he checks. Then he stops laughing. He bows, finally, very low.

events.text: A storm climbs the mountain with you. On the bare peak the air smells of iron and your hair stands up. Old manuals say a body tempered by lightning is a body that does not rot. Old manuals were written by survivors.

choices.text: Stand on the summit and take the strike

ok.log: White. Then quiet. Then your whole skin hums like a struck bell. You walk down feeling a century younger.

fail.deathCause: lightning on a bare peak, tempting heaven
fail.log: White. Then nothing. Then a long time lying on wet stone. (-25 health)

choices.text: Shelter under an overhang and watch

effects.log: The lightning walks the ridge all night. You learn its gait. That is worth something too.

events.text: You trained under this waterfall for six years, a lifetime ago. The pool is shallower now and the fall thinner. A family of otters lives in the plunge pool. They regard you as a trespasser in their bath.

choices.text: Sit under the fall again

effects.log: It hits softer than it used to. Or you are harder. The otters leave in protest and come back in curiosity.

choices.text: Catch fish for the otters

effects.log: They accept the tribute. By evening one is asleep on your foot. The waterfall never did that.

choices.text: Look for your old marks on the stone

effects.log: You find the line you scratched for each year. Six lines. Such a young number.

events.text: When you were young this was the hall of a great sect. You trembled to pass its gate. Now the gate is a goat pen. A goat stands on the founder's stone seat, chewing. The goatherd says it is a good spot for goats.

choices.text: Search the ruins

ok.log: Under a collapsed shelf, in an oiled box, a sect manual. The goats have eaten the cover and the first chapter. The rest is very good.

fail.log: A goat butts you into a ditch. You find nothing but a sense of history. (-3 health)

choices.text: Bow to the founder's seat

effects.log: The goat does not move. You bow anyway. The founder, wherever they are, would have laughed.

events.text: A map seller in the market has maps of mountains that are not there any more. One shows a pass you know fell in an earthquake a century ago. Another shows a lake that is now a rice plain. He swears they are the newest maps.

choices.text: Buy one for the history (2 taels)

effects.log: It is the world you were young in. You fold it carefully. It is the only copy of that country left.

choices.text: Sell him your corrections

effects.log: He pays twelve taels and complains every tael. Next year his maps are the best in the province.

choices.text: Tell him to let travellers find out

effects.log: He thinks this is wise. It is not. You both feel good about it anyway.

events.text: A snow lotus grows in a crevice of the glacier. It blooms once a century, and it will open in three days. You can see the petals pushing. Below, on the ice, someone else's footprints come and go. Someone is waiting too.

choices.text: Wait the three days and take it

effects.log: Three days of wind. On the fourth dawn it opens like a hand. You take it. The other footprints do not come back.

choices.text: Leave it for whoever made the footprints

effects.log: You leave a stone arrow pointing at it. Somebody young will think the heavens favour them. Let them.

choices.text: Sit with it and watch it bloom

effects.log: You watch it open and do not pick it. That is a hundred years, in one morning.

events.text: In a pawnshop hangs a scroll of calligraphy. Your calligraphy, written one drunk night a lifetime ago. The label says forgery, a cheap copy of a famous master. The price is fifteen taels. You think that is fair.

choices.text: Buy it back (15 taels)

effects.log: The strokes are wild and young. You do not write like this now. You are not sure that is good.

choices.text: Sign it again in front of the owner

effects.log: He calls the scroll appraiser. The appraiser faints. The price goes up to a thousand taels. You leave quickly.

choices.text: Laugh and leave it hanging

effects.log: It is a good forgery of you. It deserves its spot on the wall.

events.text: Winter. A wolf pack trails you through the birch woods for a day. They do not attack. The lead wolf has a white ear. You fed a grey wolf with a white ear, here, in a hungry winter long ago. Some things are carried in blood.
events.arc: The Grandchildren of the Grey Wolf

choices.text: Share your dried meat with them

effects.log: The white ear takes it from your hand, very gently, the way the old one did. The pack walks with you to the edge of the wood.

choices.text: Let them follow and say nothing

effects.log: At night they lie in a ring around your fire, just outside the light. You sleep well.

choices.text: Send them off with a flick of pressure

effects.log: They scatter. The white ear looks back once. You feel you were rude to an old friend.

events.text: Autumn in the maple valley. The leaves fall so thick the path is red. Two young sects are fighting in it, sword against sword, over a slight nobody can remember. Their best fighters are good. Their footwork is ruining the leaves.

choices.text: Stop the fight with a single word

effects.log: You say it quietly. Every sword stops. They all look at you. You suggest they look at the leaves instead.

choices.text: Watch the leaves, not the fight

effects.log: Each leaf falls its own way. None of them wins. The fight ends on its own when everyone is too tired.

choices.text: Collect the best leaves and press them

effects.log: You press them in a book. Years from now, in some inn, you will open it and have autumn again.

events.text: The temple bell has a crack down one side. You made it. You were young and wanted to test a palm strike. The monks still tell the story to novices, as a warning about anger. They do not know the culprit is on their steps.

choices.text: Pay for a new casting (20 taels)

effects.log: The abbot is amazed. The novices are disappointed. They liked the warning.

choices.text: Ring it once, gently

effects.log: It rings flat and cracked and still beautiful. The whole valley hears it. You close your eyes.

choices.text: Confess to the abbot

effects.log: The abbot laughs until he coughs. He says the warning works better now. He asks you to tell it yourself.

events.text: A mountain lake has frozen clear as glass. In the middle, under the ice, something glints, green-white and steady. The ice near it is thin and singing. Nobody from the village will walk out there. They say it is cursed.

choices.text: Cross to it on light feet

ok.log: You barely touch the ice. One palm, one crack, one cold jade the size of a fist. Behind you the ice closes like a mouth.

fail.log: The ice gives. Cold water, black and total. You come out the other side of the hole with ice in your eyebrows. (-8 health)

choices.text: Leave it under the ice

effects.log: Some things are better seen than had. The village is relieved to see you come back.

events.text: You taught a junior one stance on a hillside, a long time ago. You find the junior's grave, here, on the same hill. They lived to eighty-one. Their descendants are sweeping the grave. One of them stands in that stance.

choices.text: Help them sweep

effects.log: They thank you and offer rice wine. You pour some on the grave. You owe this one a drink.

choices.text: Correct the child's stance

effects.log: The child corrects back. "Great-grandmother said this way." Great-grandmother improved it. You learn your own stance, better.

choices.text: Watch from the trees and leave

effects.log: Eighty-one years. You were a breath in it. That is all a teacher ever is.

events.text: A night of falling stars. They streak across the sky by the dozen. One is bigger than the rest. It falls, burning, behind the ridge. You feel the ground jump under your feet a moment later.

choices.text: Run to where it fell

ok.log: A crater, smoking. In the middle, a black lump of iron still too hot to touch. You wait for dawn and take it.

fail.log: You find a smoking hole and nothing in it. A wild boar finds you. (-4 health)

choices.text: Lie back and count them

effects.log: You lose count past three hundred. You start again. You are in no hurry. You have nowhere to be.

events.text: The salt road over the hills used to be the busiest road in the south. Now it is grass, with a groove down the middle where a thousand carts wore the stone. An old woman sells boiled eggs at a crossroads where nobody passes.

choices.text: Buy every egg she has (3 taels)

effects.log: She is delighted. She tells you about her father, who had a stall here when the carts ran. You remember the stall.

choices.text: Walk the groove and listen

effects.log: Your feet find the old rhythm of the carts. For a mile you can almost hear the bells.

events.text: The inn at the pass keeps a guest ledger, every volume since it opened. The innkeeper is proud of it. You find your own entry, well over a century back, in a careless young hand: one night, one bowl of soup, paid late.

choices.text: Pay the late fee, with interest (6 taels)

effects.log: The innkeeper does the sums with real pleasure. The debt is closed in red ink. Her ancestor would be proud.

choices.text: Write a new entry under the old one

effects.log: Same name. Steadier hand. One night, one bowl of soup, paid on time. The two lines look like a teacher and a pupil.

choices.text: Read the other names from that year

effects.log: A dozen names you knew. Rivals, friends, a thief. All one night apart in the same ink. All gone but one.

events.text: The bamboo grove is flowering. It does that once in a hundred and twenty years, every stalk at once, and then the whole grove dies and grows again from seed. You saw it flower once before. You were twenty. You thought it was ordinary.

choices.text: Walk the grove while it flowers

effects.log: Pale tassels everywhere, a faint smell like rice. The grove is saying goodbye and does not seem sad about it.

choices.text: Gather seed for the next grove

effects.log: You scatter it on the bare hill across the river. In a hundred and twenty years, perhaps, you will come and look.

events.text: A bookseller presses a cheap novel into your hands. It is very popular. It is about you. In chapter one you are an orphan prince. You were not a prince. In chapter two you have a magic gourd. You have never owned a gourd.

choices.text: Buy it and read it in the inn (1 tael)

effects.log: You stay up all night. It is terrible. You want to know what happens next.

choices.text: Ask who wrote it

effects.log: "A scholar in the hill county," says the bookseller. "Never met a fighter in his life." That explains the gourd.

choices.text: Put it back on the shelf

effects.log: The bookseller sighs. Another customer picks it up behind you and buys three.

events.text: You find the novelist in the hill county. He is a thin old scholar with ink on his nose. He has no idea who you are. He is stuck on volume two: how would a great master fight a demon in a burning temple? He asks your opinion.

choices.text: Show him how it really goes

effects.log: You demonstrate in his courtyard with a broom. He writes very fast. The broom does not survive.

choices.text: Tell him he got everything wrong

effects.log: He listens carefully, nods, and keeps the gourd. "Readers love the gourd," he says. You cannot argue with that.

choices.text: Leave him in peace

effects.log: Some legends are better in their own hands. You buy his lunch on the way out.

events.text: Volume two is out. It is a sensation. In it you fight the demon with a broom, which is true, and ride a tame dragon, which is not. Young cultivators in every teahouse argue about your techniques. Some of them are doing the broom move.

choices.text: Teach the broom move properly

effects.log: A new style spreads through three provinces: the Sweeping Palm. In a hundred years it will be ancient.

choices.text: Buy a copy for the road

effects.log: The dragon gets a name in chapter nine. You decide you would have liked the dragon.

choices.text: Sit in a teahouse and listen to them argue

effects.log: They get your style wrong in eleven ways and right in one. The one is the important one. You go to bed happy.

events.text: A young genius from a famous clan hires you as a mountain guide. He thinks you are a local with good knees. He pays two taels a day, talks about himself without stopping, and is hunting a spirit beast far above his realm.

choices.text: Take the job

effects.log: Three days of climbing. You learn his whole family tree. He learns nothing about you. That suits you fine.

choices.text: Warn him off the hunt

effects.log: He laughs and hires someone else. You hope that guide has very good knees.

events.text: The beast comes out of the fog: a great horned serpent, and the young genius's sword shatters on its scales. He falls back into the scree. He shouts for you to run. It is the first time he has thought of someone else.

choices.text: Drive it off with one finger, then pretend you didn't

effects.log: He sees nothing but fog and a fleeing serpent. He thinks his shout scared it. You let him think it.

choices.text: Drive it off openly

effects.log: He watches with his mouth open. On the way down he does not talk at all. Then he asks to be taught.

choices.text: Drag him out and run, as asked

effects.log: You run like a guide. He runs like a genius, which is to say badly. You both live. He pays you double. (-4 health)

events.text: There was a mountain here. You climbed it once, at thirty, and thought it was the top of the world. Now there is a plain of broken stone, and a village at the edge that calls the place the Duel Field. Two masters did this, they say, a century ago.

choices.text: Read what the duel left in the stone

effects.log: Their whole fight is written here, one cut after another. One of them was very good. The other was better and held back.

choices.text: Plant a pine at the old summit spot

effects.log: In a thousand years it will be a small hill with a big tree. You are fairly sure you will see it.

choices.text: Sit where the peak was

effects.log: The air still remembers being high. You breathe it. Somewhere, a mountain misses itself.

events.text: What you took for a mossy stone opens its eyes. A hermit, older than you, older than anyone, moss on his shoulders like a cloak. He looks at you and smiles. "The little one who kept falling off the rope bridge," he says. He is right.

choices.text: Ask him for advice

effects.log: He says one sentence. It takes you twenty years to understand it. You understand the first word on the walk home.

choices.text: Share your qi to warm his old bones

effects.log: He hums like a kettle. He says nobody has done that in six hundred years. Then he goes back to sleep.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the bridge

effects.log: "Fell down in the year of the red comet," he says. "You were not on it. Good." He seems pleased you lived.

events.text: A small sect in the valley worships you. Their founder was a beggar you once fed. Their great statue of you has three eyes and holds a lotus and a saw. Nobody knows why the saw. The disciples bow to it four hundred times a day.

choices.text: Bow to the statue with them

effects.log: You bow to yourself four hundred times. It is surprisingly good for the back. It is also humbling.

choices.text: Ask the oldest disciple about the saw

effects.log: He explains for an hour. It is a symbol of cutting attachments. You remember now. You fixed the beggar's cart with that saw.

choices.text: Leave a blessing on their spring

effects.log: Their spring runs sweet for a century. The statue gets a fourth eye in gratitude.

events.text: At a gathering of the murim a young man of thirty stands on a table and announces he is the strongest under heaven. He has just reached a realm you passed long ago. Everyone cheers. Someone hands you a cup.

choices.text: Let him keep the title

effects.log: You drink to him. He will learn. Everybody learns, if they live, and you rather hope he does.

choices.text: Flick a peanut at his sword hand

effects.log: His sword is on the floor. The hall goes silent. You are eating another peanut. Nobody saw who threw it, except him.

choices.text: Invite him to tea afterwards

effects.log: He comes, puzzled. You talk about his master's master. He leaves very quiet, and a little better.

events.text: A vine on a cliff bears fruit once in three hundred years, and it is bearing now: three golden fruits. Under it wait a fox, a crane and a white monkey. They have been waiting a long time. They look at you with deep concern.

choices.text: Take one and leave two

effects.log: The fox nods, the crane bows, the monkey sulks. Three centuries is a long time to wait to be robbed.

choices.text: Leave all three to them

effects.log: The monkey brings you a peach a week later. Animals have long memories. So do you.

choices.text: Watch them eat theirs, then eat yours

effects.log: Four of you, sitting on a ledge, eating fruit in silence at sunset. It is the best dinner party in a century.

events.text: The great war's battlefield. Ten thousand died here, in the year you were young. Ghost fires float over the grass at dusk. The locals avoid it. You realise you are the last person alive who knows any of their names.

choices.text: Say every name you remember

effects.log: It takes until midnight. The ghost fires go out one by one. You do not know if that means anything. You hope so.

choices.text: Sit among the ghost fires

effects.log: They drift around you like curious children. They are just lights. They are not just lights.

choices.text: Raise a stone with the year on it

effects.log: Next spring a farmer leaves flowers at it. Then others. Someone else is remembering now.

events.text: In a crater at the top of a dead volcano there is a lake so still it holds the stars without a ripple. The water is so cold it hums. Nobody has climbed here in a long time; your old footprints are still in the ash.
events.arc: The Lake That Holds the Stars

choices.text: Bathe in the starlight water

effects.log: Cold to the bone, then to the marrow, then to something under the marrow. You come out shining faintly.

choices.text: Drink one handful

effects.log: It tastes of nothing at all. That is the most refreshing thing you have ever tasted.

choices.text: Step in your old footprints

effects.log: They are smaller than your feet now. No. Your feet are the same. You walked differently then.

events.text: The capital has changed its name three times since you last came. The guards at the gate demand papers. You have papers. They are from two dynasties ago, stamped by an emperor the guards learned about in school.

choices.text: Show the old papers

effects.log: The captain takes them to an archivist, who weeps. You are let in and also given lunch. They keep the papers.

choices.text: Pay the stranger's fee (5 taels)

effects.log: You are a stranger in the city you once bled for. The fee is reasonable.

choices.text: Walk over the wall in daylight

ok.log: The guards do not even see you. A child does, and tells everyone a sage walked on the wind.

fail.log: The new wall has new tricks. You pay a fine to a very smug captain. (-5 health)

events.text: Centuries ago you sealed yourself in a cave to break through. You broke through. You never came back for what you left. The seal is still there, your own seal, and it still knows you. It opens like a door you just closed.

choices.text: Go in and read your old notes

effects.log: The notes are earnest and half wrong. One margin note is brilliant. You do not remember being that clever.

choices.text: Seal it again for someone else

effects.log: You leave it for whoever finds it. Your past self would hate that. Your present self finds it funny.

choices.text: Sit in your old spot for a season

effects.log: The cave fits you like an old shoe. You leave three months later, feeling forty.

events.text: You make tea by a spring. Good water, old leaves, a cracked cup. A sparrow lands on the rim and drinks before you do. It is not afraid. Masters have shaken mountains, and you once shook a city. The sparrow does not care.

choices.text: Let it drink first

effects.log: It drinks, considers you, and leaves. You drink the rest. It is the best tea of the year.

choices.text: Stay still until it leaves on its own

effects.log: An hour. The tea goes cold. The sparrow goes to sleep. You learn more stillness than in a decade of closed door training.

events.text: You have always meant to follow the great river to its source. You do. It takes a summer. At the end, in a cave high on a mountain, it is one bead of water, dripping from a stone. Drip. Drip. That is the whole great river.

choices.text: Meditate by the drip

effects.log: Drip. A lifetime. Drip. A dynasty. Drip. You understand something about patience you thought you already knew.

choices.text: Catch one drop on your tongue

effects.log: It is cold. That drop is the whole great river. You carry it home in your belly.

events.text: You sit down on a ridge in spring meaning to rest a while. The rains come and go. The cicadas come and go. The maples redden. Snow piles on your shoulders. A deer sleeps against your back one night in winter. Spring again.

choices.text: Stand up, a year later

effects.log: Your knees are stiff. Your heart is very quiet. The deer is surprised to find it was leaning on a person.

choices.text: Stay one more year

effects.log: The second year teaches you that the first was not the same as this one. No year is. Not one.

events.text: A clan in the north holds rites every year for their great benefactor. You. You saved their founder from a flood. They think you died centuries ago. They have a tablet, incense and a very large table of food.

choices.text: Attend as a guest

effects.log: They tell you about yourself. You did more good than you remember, and less than they think.

choices.text: Reveal yourself

effects.log: Silence. An old aunt faints. A child asks if this means they still have to do the rites. They decide yes.

choices.text: Eat from the table quietly

effects.log: It is your table, technically. The rice cakes are excellent. The ancestors, somewhere, are scandalised.

events.text: Heaven's dew gathers once a decade on a stone at the far end of the Gorge of Ten Winds. The winds change every breath. They have thrown down masters of your realm before. Today they are howling like a bad mood.

choices.text: Cross the gorge for the dew

ok.log: The wind tears your sleeves off. You arrive at the stone with nothing but a jar and the dew in it. Worth it.

fail.deathCause: the Gorge of Ten Winds, a master of an earlier age
fail.log: A gust throws you into the wall, then into the next one. You crawl back. (-30 health)

choices.text: Wait for a calm day that may not come

effects.log: It does not come. But you learn the winds' order: there is one. That is better than dew.

events.text: At noon the sun goes black. The birds stop. In the village below, people bang pots to scare off the dog eating the sun. You have seen four of these. They frighten you a little less each time, and you have stopped saying so.

choices.text: Meditate on the dark sun

effects.log: For three minutes the world holds its breath. In the dark, your qi looks back at you. Then the light returns.

choices.text: Go down and calm the villagers

effects.log: You tell them it will pass. It passes. For a month you are the wise elder who ordered the sun back.

events.text: Centuries ago, angry, you cut a mountain with one stroke. The cut is still there. It is a pilgrimage site now. Young swordsmen sit in rows staring at it for enlightenment. One of them has been staring for a year.

choices.text: Watch them staring

effects.log: They see in it things you never put there. Some of those things are true. That is how teaching works, it turns out.

choices.text: Tell the year-long one it was a bad day

effects.log: He laughs for the first time in a year. Then he gets up and leaves, enlightened, sort of.

choices.text: Add a second, gentler cut beside it

effects.log: Now there are two. The pilgrims argue for a century about which is the true teaching. Both are.

events.text: A child's kite is stuck at the top of an old zelkova tree. The child is crying. You have levelled armies. The tree is very tall and the kite is very small. The child looks at you, the only adult on the road, with hope.

choices.text: Float up and fetch it

effects.log: The child stops crying and starts screaming with joy. The whole village hears about the flying grandparent by dinner.

choices.text: Climb it the ordinary way

effects.log: Bark in your hands, sap on your sleeve. You get the kite. You also get a splinter. The child is impressed by the splinter.

choices.text: Teach the child to call the wind

effects.log: It takes all afternoon. The kite comes down by itself in the end. The child thinks they did it. They did.

events.text: In a mountain market an old man sells a heap of peaches. Among the ordinary ones is one that glows a little. He does not know. He wants two taels for the basket. You could tell him. You could not.

choices.text: Buy the basket and tell him

effects.log: He goes white, keeps the glowing one, and gives you the basket for free. You pay anyway. The ordinary peaches are very good.

choices.text: Buy the basket and say nothing (2 taels)

effects.log: It tastes of years. It also tastes a little of the old man's face. You will remember both.

choices.text: Tell him and walk on

effects.log: He sells it to a magistrate for a fortune. Next year he has a shop. He names a peach after you.

events.text: Two hermits sit at a baduk board on a flat rock. Moss on the bowls. Moss on them. They have been playing one game for two hundred years and it is a tie. They look up at you with relief: a third opinion, at last.

choices.text: Suggest the winning stone

effects.log: The game ends. Both hermits stare at the board. Then they clear it and start a new one, grumbling. You have given them two more centuries.

choices.text: Decline, and watch one move

effects.log: One move takes a season. You stay for it. When the stone clicks down, the whole mountain seems to settle.

choices.text: Bring them tea and leave

effects.log: They drink it without looking up. On your way down you hear one say, "Polite youngster." You are centuries old.

events.text: In a hidden valley you find a spirit herb seedling. A thousand-year kind. It will need a century just to be worth picking. Nothing else in the world is worth waiting a century for. You are, however, very good at waiting.

choices.text: Plant a ring of stones around it

effects.log: You mark the valley on no map. You will remember. A hundred years is not so long.

choices.text: Feed it some qi before you go

effects.log: It drinks and stands up straighter. It will remember you too, in its way.

choices.text: Leave it to the valley

effects.log: Let the mountain keep it. Most good things are not for you.

events.text: A century later, you come back to the hidden valley. The herb is ripe, its leaves gold at the edges. And a young cultivator is kneeling by your stones, starving, ill, holding out a trembling hand for it. They have not seen you.

choices.text: Take it. You waited a century

effects.log: You take it. The young one looks at you with hate, then with fear, then goes. A century of waiting tastes a bit bitter.

choices.text: Give it to the young one

effects.log: They recover. In a few years someone will tell you about a master who was saved in a valley. You will say nothing.

choices.text: Split it with them

effects.log: Half a century each. You both sit by the stones afterwards. It is enough. It is always, it turns out, enough.

events.text: You find the tomb of your old rival, sealed in a hill. Their seal is weakening. It was a good seal once. They were always good at seals. They were always good at everything except beating you, and it made them furious.

choices.text: Strengthen the seal from outside

effects.log: You weave your qi into theirs. The two of you, together, for once. It feels oddly like an apology.

choices.text: Break it and go in

effects.log: The seal opens with a sigh. It was waiting for you. It always was. You step into the dark.

choices.text: Leave a cup of their favourite tea

effects.log: Bitter green tea, too strong. They would have complained. You smile and walk away.

events.text: Inside the tomb, past the traps, there is one room. In it a single scroll on a stone table, addressed to you. The one buried here knew you would outlive them. They knew you would come. The scroll is their final technique, and a note.

choices.text: Read the technique

effects.log: It is the counter to your best move. They found it at the very end. The note says: "Too late. Use it well. I win."

choices.text: Read only the note

effects.log: "You were the best of us. It was very annoying. Don't be lonely." You read it many times.

choices.text: Seal the room without reading

effects.log: Some last words are meant for nobody. You leave them their privacy, and their victory.
